title: VF-MT306-FleetObservabilityGui
clause: Flight Recorder events for reconcile passes/transitions/quarantines with tick-vs-notify trigger-source labels, native egui fleet panel with stable author_id targets showing desired vs observed per workspace, Argus inspectability

scope.summary:
GOAL: Make the fleet reconciler observable to operators and to no-context models: (1) Flight Recorder events for every reconcile pass, lifecycle transition, quarantine entry/clear, and teardown milestone, each labeled with its trigger source (BOOT | TICK | live-query change event) so drift-caught-by-tick is visible and distinguishable from event-driven work (research P8: 'log which path (tick vs notify) triggered each pass so drift-caught-by-tick is visible'); (2) a native egui fleet panel showing DESIRED vs OBSERVED state per workspace with stable author_id widget targets so parallel models can drive and read the panel deterministically; (3) Argus inspectability so the visual debug suite can capture and assert the panel.

FR EVENTS: define fleet FR event kinds following the existing FR worktree-event naming convention (FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-* family in swarm_orchestration/events.rs - MT-141's research_provenance pins those at events.rs lines 75-78 in this same WP; re-verify exact lines in the implementing worktree):
   FR-EVT-FLEET-RECONCILE-PASS { worktree_id, trigger_source, plan_summary, outcome, duration_ms, desired_generation, binding_generation }
   FR-EVT-FLEET-LIFECYCLE-TRANSITION { worktree_id, from_state, to_state, plan_step, trigger_source }
   FR-EVT-FLEET-QUARANTINE { worktree_id, entered_or_cleared, consecutive_failures, last_failure_reason }
   FR-EVT-FLEET-TEARDOWN { worktree_id, step, outcome }
   Emission points: MT-302's pass-record seam (which already carries the trigger-source label per AC-302-8), MT-303's executor transition points, MT-304's quarantine entry/clear, MT-305's finalizer steps. FR events are projections of the authoritative EventLedger records those MTs already append - never a second source of truth; where a ledger record exists, the FR event carries its reference id.

EGUI FLEET PANEL: a native egui panel (in the app's existing panel/dock system - locate the host surface in the implementing worktree app/src tree; do not invent a parallel windowing path) rendering one row per workspace within the operator's account scope:
   columns: worktree_id, desired_state (MT-301), observed lifecycle (MT-303 ObservedVmState), health_state + consecutive_failures + next_attempt_at_utc countdown (MT-304), tombstone/archive status (MT-305), last pass trigger source + timestamp, budgets (memory MiB / vcpus) and priority.
   DESIRED vs OBSERVED divergence is the panel's core visual: rows where desired != converged-observed render with a distinct emphasized style; quarantined rows render with an alert style and expose the last_failure_reason on expansion.
   Row actions (behind confirmation): set desired Running/Snapshotted, request teardown (MT-305 request_teardown), clear quarantine (MT-304 clear_quarantine). Actions call the typed store/finalizer APIs only - the panel NEVER writes SQL directly and NEVER calls the adapter.
   STABLE AUTHOR IDS: every interactive widget and every row gets a stable, deterministic author_id (e.g. fleet_panel.row.<worktree_id>.desired_select, fleet_panel.row.<worktree_id>.teardown_button, fleet_panel.summary.converged_count) so parallel models can target widgets without screen-reading (GLOBAL-BUILD-040 stable element identifiers; ids must not contain spaces and must be derivable from worktree_id alone).
   Data flow: the panel reads a FleetPanelProjection assembled backend-side (scope-filtered through the MT-301 store + registry reads); refresh on FR event arrival or a bounded poll; the panel must never block the UI thread on SurrealDB - reads go through the app's existing async bridge for backend state.
   QUIET OPERATION: the panel must not pop windows, steal focus, or hijack input when fleet events arrive (GLOBAL-BUILD-046..049); quarantine alerts surface as in-panel badges, not modal popups.

ARGUS INSPECTABILITY: register the fleet panel with the Argus visual-debug surface used by the app's GUI test flow so a model can (a) enumerate the panel's widget tree with author_ids, (b) capture a screenshot/snapshot of the panel state, (c) assert desired-vs-observed values programmatically. GUI verification per GLOBAL-BUILD-026..032: screens readable, controls discoverable, no text overlap, layout responsive, important state (divergence, quarantine) visible; record the verification path so another model can reproduce the UI test.

RESOURCE PRIVACY: the projection is assembled under the operator's ResourceAccessContext; one account's panel can never render another account's workspaces (resource_scope.rs ResourceScope 147-153; scoped list from MT-301 AC-301-4). The Argus surface exposes only the same scoped projection.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: backend - new file vm_fleet/observability.rs (FR event constructors + FleetPanelProjection assembler) and small emission-point edits in reconciler.rs/executor.rs/error_policy.rs/finalizer.rs; app - one new egui panel module + registration in the existing dock/panel registry + Argus registration; tests both sides.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read swarm_orchestration/events.rs FR kind definitions and the existing FR emission call sites; read the app's panel registry, async backend bridge, and Argus registration points in the implementing worktree.
2. Implement FR event kinds + constructors in observability.rs; wire the four emission points; carry ledger reference ids.
3. Implement FleetPanelProjection (scope-filtered, desired vs observed joined per workspace).
4. Build the egui panel with the column set, divergence/quarantine styling, stable author_ids, confirmed actions calling typed APIs.
5. Register with Argus; implement widget-tree enumeration + snapshot capture for the panel.
6. Tests: backend - FR events emitted at each point with correct trigger-source labels (live SurrealDB + fake adapter driving a pass, a transition, a quarantine, a teardown step); projection is scope-filtered (two-account test). GUI - Argus-driven test enumerates author_ids (stable across two launches), asserts divergence rendering for a desired!=observed fixture, asserts quarantine badge, executes a confirmed teardown action and observes request_teardown called; visual verification per GLOBAL-BUILD-026..032 with recorded evidence path. Spec-Realism Gate: backend events against real SurrealDB; GUI assertions through the real Argus surface, not screenshots eyeballed from memory.
7. Run proof targets; record measured output. Implementer never marks COMPLETED.
forbidden_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/src/sandbox/** (no adapter access from GUI or observability code)
acceptance_criteria: AC-306-1: FR event kinds FR-EVT-FLEET-RECONCILE-PASS / -LIFECYCLE-TRANSITION / -QUARANTINE / -TEARDOWN exist following the established FR-EVT-SWARM-* naming convention and are emitted at the four specified points, each carrying the trigger-source label (BOOT | TICK | live-query change event) where applicable.
AC-306-2: A drift scenario (state diverged with live-query change event suppressed) produces a reconcile-pass FR event labeled TICK - proving drift-caught-by-tick is distinguishable - by live test.
AC-306-3: FR events reference the authoritative EventLedger record ids they project; no FR event is the sole record of a state change (code review + test).

AC-306-4: The egui fleet panel renders desired vs observed per workspace with divergence emphasis, quarantine badges with expandable failure reason, health/backoff countdown, tombstone status, budgets, and priority.

AC-306-5: Every interactive widget and row exposes a stable author_id derivable from worktree_id alone, containing no spaces, stable across app launches - proven by an Argus enumeration test run twice.

AC-306-6: Panel actions (set desired, request teardown, clear quarantine) require confirmation and call only the typed MT-301/304/305 APIs; grep proof shows no SQL and no adapter calls in the panel module.
AC-306-7: The panel projection is account-scope-filtered; a two-account live test proves no cross-account rows render.
AC-306-8: The panel is quiet: no focus stealing, no modal popups on event arrival, no UI-thread blocking on SurrealDB (async bridge only) - verified via the Argus flow and code review.

AC-306-9: Argus can enumerate the widget tree, capture a panel snapshot, and assert divergence/quarantine state; the GUI verification evidence path (GLOBAL-BUILD-026..032 checks) is recorded so another model can reproduce it.
proof_targets: bash -lc "! grep -rnE 'official SurrealDB Rust SDK|query\(' app/src -l --include='*fleet*' && echo NO_SQL_IN_PANEL"

app/src (existing egui panel/dock registry, async backend bridge, Argus registration - locate in implementing worktree)
expected_tests: live-SurrealDB + fake adapter: each of the four FR emission points fires with correct payload and trigger label
live-SurrealDB: live-query change event-suppressed drift is caught by tick and labeled TICK
live-SurrealDB two-account test: projection scope filtering
Argus: author_id enumeration stable across two launches
Argus: divergence emphasis and quarantine badge assertions on fixtures
Argus: confirmed teardown action reaches request_teardown; unconfirmed action is a no-op

implementation_notes: IMPLEMENTATION GATE: gated on WP-1 IV verdicts + merge to main (expansion_provenance.implementation_gate); MT-302 must land first (pass-record seam), and the panel's quarantine/teardown columns degrade gracefully (render as absent) until MT-304/305 land - do not hard-depend on their columns at compile time if they have not merged.
FR events are projections; EventLedger records from MT-301..305 remain the authority (research constraint: SurrealDB/EventLedger authority only).
author_id stability is a product requirement for parallel model coordination (GLOBAL-BUILD-033..045): ids derive from worktree_id, never from row index or render order.
Trigger-source labeling exists to make resync-tick drift visible (research P8): do not collapse BOOT into TICK; they answer different diagnostic questions.
No new FR event kinds beyond the four named here without operator sign-off; payload evolution is preferred over kind proliferation (precedent: MT-141 explicitly reuses kinds and extends payloads).
All Rust including the GUI (egui); no web view, no external dashboard daemon; disk-agnostic paths; no names with spaces.

surfaces: Fleet panel (native egui): desired vs observed per workspace, divergence emphasis, quarantine badges, health/backoff countdown, tombstone status, budgets, priority, confirmed row actions

target_entries: Workspace fleet > Fleet panel (reading desired vs observed, divergence emphasis, badges, row actions)
Workspace fleet > Observability (FR event kinds, trigger-source labels, what tick-labeled drift means)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: This MT IS the FR wiring for the fleet family: four kinds, trigger-source labeled, ledger-referenced. The MT-302..305 DEFERRED-to-MT-306 notes resolve here.
Panel projection assembly failures and Argus registration failures emit diagnostic events via the open diagnostic-event API if present; otherwise DEFERRED-with-reason.
Observability/GUI MT; the daemon's liveness posture is recorded in MT-302. The panel itself is in-app UI with no separate process.

risk_if_missed: The fleet is a black box: operators cannot see desired-vs-observed divergence or quarantines, drift caught by the resync tick is indistinguishable from event-driven work (masking event-path bugs, the exact P8 warning), and parallel models have no stable widget targets - forcing fragile screen-reading against GLOBAL-BUILD-045.

risks: RISK-1: FR events become a second source of truth that drifts from EventLedger records, so replay and panel disagree.
RISK-2: Panel actions write SQL or call the adapter directly, bypassing scope enforcement, generation fencing, and intent journaling.
RISK-3: author_ids derive from row order and reshuffle every refresh, breaking every parallel-model automation built on them.
RISK-4: The panel renders cross-account workspaces through an unscoped projection query.
RISK-5: Quarantine alerts pop modal/focus-stealing UI while models are driving the app, violating quiet-operation rules.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): FR events carry ledger reference ids and are emitted only where a ledger record exists (AC-306-3).
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Actions restricted to typed APIs; grep proof no SQL/adapter in panel module (AC-306-6).
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): author_ids derive from worktree_id alone; two-launch stability test (AC-306-5).
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Projection assembled under ResourceAccessContext; two-account test (AC-306-7).
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): In-panel badges only; Argus flow + code review verify no focus steal or modal on event arrival (AC-306-8).

surrealdb_translation_v02_205.schema_rule: Any embedded PostgreSQL DDL/SQL snippet is a semantic field/index/invariant inventory only. Implement it as SCHEMAFULL SurrealQL through SurrealKit; do not execute or mechanically transliterate the snippet.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.concurrency_rule: Translate advisory locks, SKIP LOCKED and row locks into SurrealDB transactions, durable lease/fencing records and conditional updates with equivalent tests.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.notification_rule: Translate LISTEN/NOTIFY into scoped SurrealDB live queries plus bounded resynchronization.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.privacy_rule: Translate RLS into authenticated record-user table/field PERMISSIONS intersected with ResourceBroker; administrative credentials cannot prove privacy.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.proof_rule: All named storage proofs run against real SurrealDB. No PostgreSQL process, driver, connection, fixture, environment variable or fallback is permitted.
